Daisy Island Station is a station on East Ring Line. It is operated by Nazca Railway (Los Sengas Division), and is located at Los Sengas Egress. This station will serve Luxter Line, Origin Line, Fox Line and Kilo Line in the future.

Station Title and Soundtrack[]

  • The Station Title of this Station is Garden Eden.
  • This Station features two soundtracks that belong to the album "Of Soil and Splendor, Of Jest and Joy".
Name of the Soundtrack Length (mm:ss)
Garden Eden 01:30

Fun Facts[]

  • The design of this station alludes to Banyan Station with regards that a large concourse is followed by smaller platforms above it.
  • Colored Stained Glass corresponding to the color of the line appears on all platforms behind the tracks.
  • It took the railway builder an hour and a half to place the all black ImageOnMap Signs reserved for future use at this station.[6]
  • From the outside of this station, it can be seen that the platform numbers increase in a clockwise direction starting from the East Ring Line Platforms.
  • Similar to Gentle Island Station and Snowdan Island Station, this station is named after the fact that it is situated on an Island.
  • Originally, this station had plans to serve Alpha Line instead of Kilo Line. However, upon further consideration, as Luxter Line, Origin Line and Fox Line all served Sand Martin Checkpoint as well, having Alpha Line in this station would mean unnecessary repetition of lines. As a result, in order to secure the transferability of different routes, Kilo Line is used instead.[7]
  • Among all the Stations built in Season 3 Episode 11 that have known plans to become interchange stations, this station is the only station that still remains a single-line station to this day. However, among all the stations in the same episode, this station is also the first station to get its Station Title Banner and complete its Station Title and Icon Upgrade Scheme. The other known interchange Stations built in Season 3, Episode 11 are as follows:
    • Wilde Street Station: Became an Interchange in Season 3, Episode 16 with the establishment of Pegasus Line on February 14 2022, one year and eight months after it began services alongside Origin Line on May 19 2020.
    • Bondhill Curves Station: Became an Interchange in Season 3, Episode 14 Part 2 with the establishment of Glinstrouß Line on July 16 2021, one year and 27 days after it began services alongside Daring Line on June 19 2020.
    • Centopia: Became an Interchange in Season 3, Episode 12 with the extension of Alpha Line on July 27 2020, just 19 days after it began services alongside Daring Line on July 8 2020. It would go on to serve Utopia Line on May 19 2021, 315 days after it first began services, Sparkling Line on November 19 2023, three years and four months after it began services and Zephyr Line on December 18 2023, three years and five months after it began services.
    • Quillow Terrace Station: Became an Interchange in Season 3, Episode 14 Part 2 with the extension of New Edward Line on September 7 2021, 419 days after it began services alongside Daring Line on July 15 2020.
    • Le Monde Station: Upgraded into a Checkpoint in Season 3, Episode 14 Part 2 with the arrivals of Bravo Line, New Edward Line and Akashi Line on August 27 2021, September 7 2021 and October 7 2021 respectively, with Bravo Line arriving just 405 days after it began services and two days after it became a Checkpoint.

This makes Daisy Island Station the only known interchange in Season 3, Episode 11 that is currently still a single-line station.

Future Development[]

  • This station will become a Checkpoint once Luxter Line, Origin Line and Fox Line extends from Sand Martin Checkpoint to this station and Kilo Line extends from Pi Lake Station to this station.

History[]

  • June 5 2020: This station began services alongside East Ring Line, but Luxter Line, Origin Line, Fox Line and Kilo Line Platforms remain reserved.
  • March 23 2023: The Station Title Banner of this station is added.
  • January 3 2025: This station completed its Station Title and Icon Upgrade Scheme.[8]

Dansein is one of the Sub-Districts of Peckern North. The two new development areas within this district is mainly designed for resdiential and commercial use. This area is developed by DaOrangeStoneOre.

History[]

Dansein Market[]

Dansein was originally named "K-Paifay", and a station was set up by Cities Transport Railway Division on December 2017. However, due to the fact that the Chinese name of that area had innuendos, the station at that area was re-named Dansein Market Station on September 2018. Afterwards, residential and commercial development begun around that station, and twelve grids were defined at the area closest to this station. However, the grids have yet to see any development to date.

Subsequent development to the southwest of Dansein Market is the Shek Pai Tau New Town and what will become Tin Kam. While the area developed at the southwest is derived from the potential development in the Dansein Market area, the developer became worried that new town development would affect scenery near Dansein Market.

Gremming[]

Gremming is a forest located between Dansein Market and Shek Pai Tau New Town, and it may be dervied from the word "Gremlin", which is a "mischievous folkloric creature responsible for malfunctions in aircraft, and later in other machinery, processes, and their operators".

However, the reason why the area was related to "Gremlin" in the first place is in turn related to a certain villager named Gamil who lived in Clearbrook Village. He was wandering around where Gamil Court is today when he suddenly began reminiscing about his life and screamed erratically. Nearby villagers were alerted of this commotion and upon discovering, only to find his body. As a result, that area was named "Gremming" to commemorate the dead villager.

Just a few days after Shek Pai Tau New Town began construction, Gremming Forest was razed down, and in its place were public housing. Currently, this area is riddled with a series of public housing that is home to 76 thousand people. If subsequent construction of private housing were considered, the population of this area totals 160 thousand.

Pan Tin[]

Named after the Village of Pan Tin Tsuen, the area northwest of Dansein Market was once resided with citizens, known of their elegant lifestyles.

Upon the beginning of development of Dansein, the residents agreed with a compensated transfer of land ownership for residential development, under the conditions of resettlement within the area and a control in residential building counts. With that in mind under comprehensive planning, the upper limit of 39 public residential buildings were set by the developers (by symbolic derivations from the Chinese characters of the name Pan Tin). The planning also included the construction of Pan Tin Court in fulfillment of the resettlement condition.

Following the initializing in development of Northern Dansein New Town, the developers changed their plans to break free of the 39 buildings limit. Though the native residents of Pan Tin welcomed the change, and hoped an increase to the developments of housing developments for home ownership, in combat to the nearby private housing developments.

Currently the west potion of the area is generally completed, while that of the east is still under construction.

Summary[]

Contrary to the perceived priorities implied by the naming, the surrounding housing development of this area is more well-developed than the centered "market" area.

Future Development[]

After the facilities for the existing Public Housing Estates are completed, Dansein will expand to the northwest at the outside, and the "Dansein Residential Area" would be further divided into "South Dansein" and "North Dansein" residential areas.

In response to re-development of the nearby Tin Kum-Shek Pai Tau New Town, plans to integrate Dansein and Shek Pai Tau into a larger-scaled Peckern North Metropolis are also in place.

Fun Facts[]

  • The last words of the Chinese name of this station refers to a branch of waterways and is usually used at location names.[2] While the English names of places that involved that word are mostly Homophonic Translations (Such as Tai Po Kau in Hong Kong and Beijiao in Shunde), as Homophonic Translations are not viable for Nazca Railway, the word "Joint" was proposed as a result due to the fact that a branch of waterways can also be seen as a joint of waterways.[3]
  • To allude to the theme of this station, bodies of water are seen at the ceiling and floorboards of the concourse.

History[]

  • August 21 2018: This Station began services.
  • April 5 2024: Exit E is added to this station to connect to Peckern North LRT Dansein Joint Stop.

Dansein Joint Stop is a stop of Tin Kam Line. It is operated by Nazca Railway Peckern North LRT, and is located at Los Sengas Peckern North Dansein. Passengers may also use this station to change to Nazca Railway Arcgo Line (Dansein Joint Station).

Dansein Market Station is a station on Arcgo Line and Glinstrouß Line. It is operated by Nazca Railway (Los Sengas Division), and is located at Los Sengas Peckern North. Passengers may also use this station to change to Peckern North LRT Tin Kam Line (Dansein Market Stop) and Cities Transit Peckern City Circular (Dansein Market Station).

Fun Facts[]

  • This station shares structure, exit numbers and fare zones with Cities Transit Peckern City Circular Dansein Market Station. As the Cities Transit part was constructed first, the exit numbers of this station starts with the letter G.
  • If Spin-offs are considered, this station is the last station to be built in Season 2.
  • Due to residential and commercial plans, the Cities Transit station platform width is of an even number. As Nazca Railway uses odd numbers as platform widths for convention, the station structure has to be moved to the west by one block with reference to the symmetry line.
  • The Arcgo Line Platforms of this station uses Side Platforms, whereas Pingsing Station and Dansein Joint Station uses Island Platforms. This arrangement alludes to the Island Line westbound extension between Kennedy Town Station and Sheung Wan Station.[3] This is due to the fact that the Cities Transit section of this station opened first, and in order to better share structures, the side platforms are used.
  • The color scheme of this station alludes to FamilyMart.
  • As the East Side and West Side Structures of Dansein Market Stop are separated in a fashion similar to Ivan City Station and Aest Station, The Concourse of this Station is used as a means of Connection between the these two structures.

History[]

  • August 22 2018: This station completed construction.
  • August 23 2018: This station began services alongside Arcgo Line. [4]
  • July 9 2021: The Glinstrouß Line part of this station began extension.
  • July 11 2021: The Glinstrouß Line platforms and concourse part of this station completed expansion.
  • July 16 2021: Glinstrouß Line is established.
  • April 20 2024: Connecting Passageways are built for access to Peckern North LRT Dansein Market Stop.

Description[]

Daring Line is one of the Auxiliary Lines of Nazca Railway Los Sengas Division.

This route is represented by the Gold Color on the Nazca Railway Route Map, and is Line Number 10.

Currently, this route is 21.93 km long, with a total of 13 stations.

Line Characteristics[]

  • The first line to NOT serve the Los Sengas Continent in Nazca Railway Los Sengas Division.
  • This line is named after the nickname of a former administrator in this server, and the Chinese name is simply the translation by the pronounciation.
  • The main purpose of this line in Peckern Continent is to interchange with other main lines. As a result, in order to collaborate with West Ring Line and Stadium Line in the form of cross-platform interchange, the line adopts a "Right-Hand Traffic" Rule.
  • In Peckern North, this line aims to assist Arcgo Line Services to the west of Dansein Market Station and around the area of Shek Pai Tau.
  • After leaving Peckern Continent, this line would enter Centopia, before entering Twenty-Second Continent to serve the development area there.

title: Dark Pearl Transit System
safeHtml:
Dark Pearl Transit System is the Light Rail System on Dark Pearl Island. It is ran by Mushroom Transit.

Station List[]

Currently, Dark Pearl Transit System has two lines with ten stations as follows:

  • Pearl Ring Line (Green)
    • Chu Ying Wui Station
    • Dark Pearl Coast Station
    • Darkourst City Station
    • Nam Ting Station (Interchange with SLT Line 502 Dark Pearl Island Stop)
    • Dark Pearl Pier Station (Interchange with Kneelearl Bypass)
    • Tung Bui Station (Interchange with Peckern Transit Northland Line Dark Pearl Island Station)
    • Bung Chu Kok Station
    • Hau Tei Fong Station (Interchange with Kneelearl Bypass)

After Hau Tei Fong Station, Pearl Ring Line will go back to Chu Ying Wui Station.

  • Kneelearl Bypass (Dark Gray)
    • Hau Tei Fong Station (Interchange with Pearl Ring Line)
    • Heiseio Station
    • Dark Pearl Pier Station (Interchange with Pearl Ring Line)
    • Westay Isle (Gate) Station
    • Kneeling Island Station

Station Souvenir Hints[]

 The following text contains large amounts of spoilers. Read with caution.
  • Stars: 1
  • Walk to the North End of Platform 2
  • The Station Souvenir comes in the form of a Gold Ingot.

Fun Facts[]

  • Orange Wool is used in this station to allude to the theme of "Dawn" in order to give this station a warm color scheme while making players feel refreshed.[2]
  • All Exits and Platforms of this station face to the east in a fashion similar to Johnson Views Station in order to correspond to the concept of "Dawn".
  • Among the "East Ring Line Loop Completion Series" Stations, this station is the only station that adopts Stacked Side Platforms. Platform 1 of this station is narrower than that of Platform 2 as Passengers for Inner Ring Trains have to pass through Platform 2 before reaching Platform 1. The wider platforms at Platform 2 facilitiates passenger flow.
  • In terms of Distance, this station is the furthest and on the opposite side from Metropolis Terminal.

History[]

  • September 23 2017: This Station completed construction.[3]
  • September 24 2017: This station began services.
  • May 21 2020: The East Ring Line Branch between Lower Shack Station and Daisy Island Station began services from this station.

Description[]

Daybreaker Line is one of the District Lines of Nazca Railway Los Sengas Division. It passes through TriPaw, Oasis and Prymea.

This line is represented by Dark Orange on the Nazca Railway Route Map, and is Line Number 31.

Currently, this route is 22.33 km long, with a total of 17 stations.

History[]

Development Chapters[]

  • S3E12: Firewood Point - Old Brightland
  • S3E17: Firewood Point - Upper Oasis
  • S4E10: Firewood Point - Spring Point (Line Complete)

Nazca Railway 2021 Development Outline[]

Direction Development Details Progress
Up Extend Eastwards from Old Brightland Checkpoint to Oasis, where it interchanges with other lines. Completed
(Chapter: S3E17+S4E10)

Nazca Railway Development Plan 2024 Edition[]

Direction Development Details Progress
Up Extend Southeast from Upper Oasis Station to Spring Point Gateway through Blue Swamp Station and Backcomma Beach Station. Completed
(Chapter: S4E10)

Districts Served[]

  • TriPaw
  • Oasis
  • Prymea

Line Characteristics[]

  • One of the District Lines of Nazca Railway Los Sengas Division. This line mainly serves TriPaw and Oasis, especially areas in TriPaw that are previously inaccessible by Akashi Line and other Nazca Railway lines.

Fun Facts[]

  • This line was born due to the fact that the original Akashi Line plans took too many detours in TriPaw.
  • Despite passing through West Ring Line, Urban Line and Minecraft Line, this line does not interchange with any of these lines.
  • This line, along with Vision Line, serves as the Auxiliary Lines of Akashi Line. This line is responsible for alleviating transport needs in the TriPaw area, as well as serving as the connection from TriPaw to east Los Sengas.

Decajotine Island Station is a station on Gondola Line. It is operated by Nazca Railway (Los Sengas Division), and is located at Los Sengas Decajotine Island. Passengers may also use this station to change to Peckern Transit Northland Line (Decajotine Island Station) and Decajotine System Line A (Hub Station).

Fun Facts[]

  • The original plans of the Gondola Line involved the trains stopping at Cajotine Island Station instead and did not involve this station. However, due to insufficient space on Cajotine Island upon investigation, plans to set up a station on that island were ultimately scrapped, and trains would go here instead.[2]
  • This Station is the first Oceanfloor Station ever built. Oceanfloor Stations are characterised by the fact that the platform struutre is usually located on or under the seabed. However, concourses of these stations are usually located at the mainland area of the landmass or the island at which the station is located. This gives the railway builder a more flexible approachr regarding the construction of the concourse in case of limited space on the island.[3]

History[]

  • October 25 2018: The Platforms of this station completed construction.[4]
  • October 28 2018: This Station began services. Gondola Line is established.

safeHtml:
Decajotine System is the Light Rail System on Decajotine Island. It is ran by Cities Transit Railway Division.

Station List[]

Currently, Decajotine System has two lines with eight stations as follows:

  • Line A:
    • Hub Station (Interchange with Nazca Railway Interisland Line, Peckern Transit Northland Line)
    • Decas Station
    • Central Station (Interchange with Line B)
    • Northaway Station
    • Sepaway Station (Interchange with Line B)
    • Viewbay Station

After Viewbay Station, Line A will go back to Hub Station.

  • Line B:
    • Sepaway Station (Interchange with Line A)
    • Central Station (Interchange with Line A)
    • Northasung Station
    • Southarole Station

December 9 is the 343rd day of the year (344th in leap years) in the Gregorian Calendar.

Historical Events[]

2017[]

2020[]

  • Nazca Railway Glacier Line Lucky Pit Station began operations.
  • Coopol became District 30 of Los Sengas.

2022[]

  • Nawis Railway Snow White Line Kum Kei Wan Station began operations.
  • Nawis Railway Snow White Line extends to Potato Farmland Station. Snow White Line completed construction.

Deepond Island (Ch: 深湖洲, Jp: 深湖洲・Fukaumi-shima) is one of the islands on West Metropolis Archipelago. It is located to the south of Inthree Island, the southeast of Axtail Island and the southwest of Coubird-Flask Group. It features a Nazca Railway Station featuring Arcgo Line and Interisland Line for external access. However, due to historical reasons, development on this island was temporarily suspended before resuming on May 8 2019.

Location[]

Deepond Island is located at the northwest of West Metropolis Archipelago. It houses a deep pond named Deepond and is the namesake of this island.

East Pond Reef[]

East Pond Reef is one of the subsidiary reefs of Deepond Island, and is separated from Deepond Island by Lighthouse River.

Geological Points of Interest[]

  • Deepond
  • Hai-Kau River
  • Lighthouse River

Map[]


Transport Manual[]

Arriving from east Los Sengas
  • After Using /spawn or arriving at Metropolis Terminal, take Delta Line to Jayler Station, and then change to Arcgo Line before alighting at Deepond Island Station.
  • Passengers from northeast Los Sengas may directly take Arcgo Line and alight at Deepond Island Station.
Arriving from Peckern, Caver Island, Heeled Island, Stem Island, Note Group, Kneeling Island, Dark Pearl Island
  • Take West Ring Line to Fansim Island Station, and then change to Arcgo Line before alighting at Deepond Island Station.
  • Passengers from Stone Shoal or Stadium Line Stations to the west of it are advised to change to SLT Line 801 at Stone Shoal Station, before changing to West Ring Line at Gull Woods Station before reaching Fansim Island Station. The rest of the journey is the same as above.
Arriving from Axhead Island, Axtail Island, Flask Island, Bufly Island
  • Tourists are advised to take ships from Nazca Ferry or use the Elytra to fly to the island.
Arriving from Threeler, Ponsand Island, Ponrest Island, Peckern North
  • Tourists are advised to take ships from Nazca Ferry or use the Elytra to fly to the island.
Arriving from other stations along Stadium Line, New Edward Line, Interisland Line
  • Tourists are advised to use Interisland Line to reach to this station.

Sub-Districts[]

Deepond Island is divided into 10 Sub-Districts as follows:

  • Deepnorth (Japanese:深北町(ふかきたちょう)): Located near Exit B of the Nazca Railway Station, and includes the Nazca Ferry. It was formerly named North Pond, and development of this sub-district is mostly complete save for a few buildings.
  • Grand Pond (Japanese:大湖町(だいこちょう)): Located near the south of Deepnorth to the North coast of Deepond. It is currently planned as a commercial district.
    • The japanese name is named after an area in Neihu District of Taipei with the same name.
  • North Sand (Japanese:北砂町(きたすなちょう)): Located to the west of Deepnorth. It is home to the Deepond Island Government. Its development is mostly complete.
  • Grass Pond (Japanese:草湖町(くさこちょう)): A peninsula to the northwest of Deepond. It is currently planned to be a commercial district.
  • West Pond (Japanese:西湖町(さいこちょう)): Located at the west of Deepond Island and the south of Grass Pond. It is currently planned to have public facilities, including a library, a hospital and a school. It is currently the main development area of the island.
    • The japanese name is named after an area in Neihu District of Taipei with the same name.
  • Star Pond (Japanese:星湖町(ほしみずうみちょう)): Located at the northeast of Deepond Island. it is currently a residential area, and is undergoing re-construction.
  • East Pond (Japanese:東湖町(とうこちょう)): A thin strip of land to the east of Deepond Island. It features a Fish Market, a Post Office and a Campsite. The proposed Route 12 exit is also located here.
    • The japanese name is named after an area in Neihu District of Taipei with the same name.
  • East Coast (Japanese:東岸町(とうがんちょう)): A new reclaimation area to the east of Star Pond. It features a lighthouse and a market. It is planned to be a commercial-residential district in the future.
  • Gravies (Japanese:グラビ): Located at the south of Deepond Island. Formerly named South Pond, this area is planned to be a residential district, and is currently one of the main development areas. It is also home to Deepond Light Rail's depot.
    • The english name is named after the first area developed by Haruna City Railway on February 2015.
  • Godplains/Kamibara (Japanese:神原町(かみばらちょう)): A shoal located at the southeast of Deepond Island. It is the tourist hotspot of Deepond Island, and is also home to the bus terminal.

Transport[]

Nazca Railway[]

  • Arcgo Line, Interisland Line Deepond Island Station

Deepond Light Rail[]

More info on this chatper could be seen at Deepond Light Rail.

Besides of Nazca Railway, another major transport infrastructure within Deepond Island is the Deepond Light Rail. Deepond Light Rail is an in-district rail system operated jointly by the Deepond Island Government and the Deepond Light Rail Management Company. Currently, it is under re-construction.

Maritime Transport[]

  • At the north of this island, the Deepond Island Pier ran by Nazca Ferry Co. Ltd. is constructed, and is colloquially named "North Pier". Passengers can use this pier to reach islands such as Coubird-Flask Group, Droplet Island, Axhead Island, Axtail Island and Bufly Island.
  • At the south of this island, the Gravies Street Pier is also present. It is currently a historic site of Deepond Island. To the south of this island is a freight terminal which is colloquially named "South Pier".

Roads[]

  • Beneath this island, a Public Transport Interchange for Route 12 is constructed, with a station (Route 12 Entrance Station) that is served by Deepond Light Rail Line 4 and will be served by Line 6.

Buses[]

Deepond Underground Walkway[]

More info on this chatper could be seen at Deepond Underground Walkway.

Deepond Underground Walkway is constructed by the Deepond Island Government in order to help citizens adopt to the adverse weather. However, due to redevelopment, most of the underground walkway have been demolished.

Points of Interest[]

Future Development[]

Deepond Island will become a mid-density residential area complete with its own underground walkway and sewer systems.

Deepond Island Station is a station on Arcgo Line and Interisland Line. It is operated by Nazca Railway (Los Sengas Division), and is located at Los Sengas Deepond Island. Passengers may also use this station to change to Deepond Light Rail Line 1 North Pond, Line 1, Line 3 East Pond, Line 3, Line 4 Kamibara and Line 1, Line 5 Gravies Stations.

Station Souvenir Hints[]

 The following text contains large amounts of spoilers. Read with caution.
  • Stars: 1
  • One player is enough
  • Find a Deep Pond at the Platform 2 Lobby
  • Trust the force and swim downwards.
  • Be careful once you reach the bottom. If you ended up to the sides you would end up in the Void.
  • The Station Souvenir comes in the form of dyed potion.

Fun Facts[]

  • For all Arcgo Line Stations within West Metropolis Archipelago, a body of water behind a pane of glass is used for identification. In this station, the pane of glass is located on the floor.
  • While Interisland Line originally intended to serve Inthree Island Station, as doing so would mean that the station would lose the property of "3", Interisland Line ended up serving this station instead.
  • This station is the last station to undergo expansion in 2017.
  • The in-station transit for this station is not built until the addition of Exits D to F.
  • This station features the first in-station transit to feature more than one distinct line (North-South Line, East-West Line).[4]

History[]

  • December 16 2015: This station began services alongside Arcgo Line.
  • September 23 2016: This station finished Upgrading Works.[5]
  • July 12 2017: This station began and completed the Interisland Line expansion. At the same day, Interisland Line extends from Elevate Island Station to this station.
  • June 29 2018: This station finished Second Stage Upgrading Works.[6]
  • June 16 2022: This station completed exit naming.[7]
  • September 23 2023: This station completed the concourse expansion, and Exit E is added to this station.
  • September 24 2023: The Deepond Island In-Station Transit completed construction, and Exits D, F are added to this station.
  • August 7 2024: The Station Banners of this station are set up.[8]

title: Deepond Light Rail
safeHtml:
Deepond Light Rail is the Light Rail System on Deepond Island, it is operated by Haruna City Railway.

Contents

  • 1 Station List
    • 1.1 Current Lines
    • 1.2 Abolished Stations
  • 2 Depots
  • 3 Sidings
  • 4 Gallery
  • 5 Citations and References

Station List[]

Currently, Deepond Light Rail has six lines with 31 stations.

Current Lines[]

  • Line 1: Formally named Island Ring Line. It is one of the main lines of Deepond Light Rail. The stations of this line are as follows:
    • North Pond Station (Interchange with Nazca Railway Arcgo Line, Interisland Line)
    • Deepond City Hall Station (Interchange with Line 5)
    • Kong Pond Station
    • Inner Pond Station
    • West Pond Station (Interchange with Line 4)
    • Gravies Station (Interchange with Line 5 and Nazca Railway Arcgo Line, Interisland Line)
    • East Pond Station (Interchange with Line 3 and Nazca Railway Arcgo Line, Interisland Line)
    • Hai-Kou River Station (Interchange with Line 2)
    • Star Pond Station (Interchange with Line 3)

After Star Pond Station, Line 1 will go back to North Pond Station.

  • Line 2: Formally named Grand Pond Line. It opened on May 27 2025. The stations of this line are as follows:
    • Deepond Lighthouse Station (Interchange with Line 3, Line 6)
    • Hai-Kou River Station (Interchange with Line 1)
    • Grand Pond Station
    • Watorest Station (Interchange with Line 5)
    • Deepond School Station (Opened on July 24 2025, Interchange with Line 4)
  • Line 3: Formally named East Pond Line. It opened on June 20 2023 as an Eastern Vertical link connecting the two piers on Deepond Island. The stations of this line are as follows:
    • Deepond South Pier Station
    • Kamibara Station (Interchange with Line 4 and Nazca Railway Arcgo Line, Interisland Line)
    • East Pond Station (Interchange with Line 1 and Nazca Railway Arcgo Line, Interisland Line)
    • East Coast Road Station
    • East Coast Reef Station (Interchange with Line 6)
    • Deepond Lighthouse Station (Interchange with Line 2, Line 6)
    • Star Pond East Station
    • Star Pond Station (Interchange with Line 1)
    • Deepond North Pier Station
  • Line 4: Formally named West Pond Line. It opened on June 4 2023 as a horizontal link at the south of Deepond Island. The current stations of this line are as follows:
    • Route 12 Entrance Station (Will interchange with Line 6)
    • Kamibara Tourist Area Station
    • Kamibara Station (Interchange with Line 3 and Nazca Railway Arcgo Line, Interisland Line)
    • South Pond Station (Interchange with Line 5)
    • Tai Wah Station
    • West Pond Station (Interchange with Line 1)
    • Kau Po Station (Opened on May 27 2025)
    • Deepond School Station (Opened on July 24 2025, Interchange with Line 2)
    • Kusanari Station (Opened on July 24 2025)
    • Grasspond Station (Opened on July 24 2025, Interchange with Line 5)
    • Jatus Station (Opened on July 24 2025)
  • Line 5: Formally named Watorest Line. It opened on March 15 2023 as the vertical link of Deepond Island. The stations of this line are as follows:
    • Grasspond Station (Opened on July 24 2025, Interchange with Line 4)
    • Deepond City Hall Station (Interchange with Line 1)
    • Watorest Station (Will interchange with Line 2)
    • Kangning Station
    • Gravies Station (Interchange with Line 1 and Nazca Railway Arcgo Line, Interisland Line)
    • South Pond Station (Interchange with Line 4)
    • Axview Station (Opened on July 24 2025)
  • Line 6: Formally named Sham Yang Line. It opened on November 26 2025 as the vertical link of East Deepond Island. The stations of thsi line are as follows:
    • Route 12 Entrance Station (Interchange with Line 4)
    • Route 12 Monitoring Post Station
    • East Coast Reef Station (Interchange with Line 3)
    • Deepond Lighthouse Station (Interchange with Line 2 and Line 3)
    • Umigake Station

Abolished Stations[]

  • Line 1 North Sand Bay Station
  • Line 1 Heaping Shoal Station

Depots[]

  • Kamibara Depot
  • Jatus Depot

Sidings[]

  • Heaping Shoal Sidings (Line 1, Line 3)
  • Hai-Kou Sidings (Line 2)
  • North Pier Sidings (Line 3)
